t: The same buyer, four aisles apart.
d: The Microplastic Auditor is sold a toothbrush by Primals, a frying pan by HexClad, gym shorts by Nero and dishwasher tablets by Blueland — all on the same lever: this ordinary object has been poisoning you. Nothing in the product connects them. The anxiety does.

t: Blame relocation is the highest-yield lever on the page.
d: The Self-Blamer Let Off The Hook shows up in ten brands across hormones, focus, testosterone, skincare and socks. Every one of them says a version of it was never your discipline. It is the most reliably long-running argument in this corpus.

t: Proof is a genre, not a claim.
d: The Sceptic Who Wants A Diagram spans fourteen brands and nine categories — a lab coat at Ulike, a Venn diagram at Blueland, an exploded outsole at The North Face, a stainless-steel Q&A at Caraway. The buyer does not want the benefit. They want to be shown the mechanism.

t: Hormones are the villain. Both sexes.
d: Cortisol, testosterone, peri-menopause. Same job in six brands: move the cause of a body you dislike from your behaviour to your biology. Happy Mammoth, Primal Queen and Mars Men are one psychographic in three costumes. It isn't my fault, and the mechanism has a name.

The patient whose appetite vanished. The one with constipation. The man refusing injections. Huel, Grüns, Primal Queen and Mars Men each serve one of them. Three buyers, one drug. Treat it as a single audience and you leave two unserved.

Lab coats at Primal Queen and Resilia. Doctor reacts at Ulike. A real cancer researcher. Yale-educated scientists. Not one of them works for the advertiser. The buyer distrusts their own doctor and trusts a credentialed dissenter.
We made too much. We really fcked up this time. Apologies to last week's buyers. Frame the discount as a mistake and the price drops without the product being worth less.

RŌZ's longest runner is a checkout screen reading Due Today $0.00. Norse Organics makes its returns policy the efficacy claim: acne will never return. Where price is the objection, don't pay yet beats pay less.
